name: PA-09
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Dan Meuser running for re-election with a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Republican win at about 97%
No public polling or expert ratings to shift the picture
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Meuser: a heavily Republican seat, incumbency, and a fundraising advantage over Wallace, with markets pricing a Republican win near certainty. No polls or ratings justify moving away from that baseline.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a tighter race or a surge of Democratic outside spending would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Dan Meuser seeks re-election in a northeastern Pennsylvania district that leans about nineteen points Republican, making this one of the safer Republican-held House seats on the map. Meuser has raised roughly $1.9 million and holds a cash advantage over Democratic challenger Rachel Wallace, who has raised about $700,000, much of it late in the cycle.

No public general-election polling or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets price a Republican win at about 97 percent, consistent with a comfortable double-digit Meuser victory.
